chunks: He said: Abu Ghalib Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Zurari reported to us, saying: My grandfather Muhammad ibn Sulaiman narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Asim ibn Humaid, from Abu Ubaidah al-Hadhdha', who said: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both) saying: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:

Indeed, the good deed quickest in reward is righteousness, and the evil deed quickest in punishment is oppression. And it is enough of a fault for a person that he sees in others what he is blind to in himself, that he reproaches people for what he himself cannot abandon, and that he harms his companion with what does not concern him.
ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about righteousness and seeing faults in others?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition, transmitted through Imam al-Baqir (AS), combines two complementary teachings. The first establishes a moral principle about divine recompense: righteousness (birr) brings the swiftest reward from God, while oppression (baghy) brings the swiftest punishment. The second teaching addresses three character flaws: hypocrisy in moral judgment, reproaching others for one's own faults, and meddling in others' affairs.
